assessment: In this elegant and rigorous study, the authors investigated the neural correlates of planning and execution of single finger presses in a 7T fMRI study focusing on primary somatosensory (S1) and motor (M1) cortices. BOLD patterns of activation/deactivation and finger-specific pattern discriminability indicate that M1 and S1 are involved not only during execution, but also during planning of single finger presses. These important results clearly establish that the role of primary somatosensory cortex goes beyond pure processing of tactile information and will be of great interest for researchers in the field of motor control and of systems neuroscience.
